title: Smudging after a few paint strokes never freezes the app
goal: After painting a few strokes (watercolour among them), starting to smudge froze Photonz. Smudging, and any edit after painting, should respond at once however many strokes are on the layer.
notes: User, 2026-10-25: 'after a few paint strokes i tried to smudge and it froze the app'. Sampled the dev app (pid 30388) right after: about 82% CPU, then 0% a few seconds later, so it recovered. The main thread was not blocked during the 3 s sample. Background tile renders (EditorState.refreshCrispTile, EditorState.swift:5629 -> DocumentRenderer.renderTile -> DocumentRenderer.raster(for:) DocumentRenderer.swift:345 -> PaintRasterizer.rasterize/paint PaintRasterizer.swift:52/112) were re-running WatercolourStroke.mark for whole strokes (Watercolour.swift:153-175, WetField.ensure :319). Theory, not confirmed: an edit to the paint layer throws its raster away and re-simulates every stroke from scratch, possibly once per tile, so the canvas stops updating until that finishes. The full sample is queue/audits/2026-10-25-smudge-freeze-sample.txt. Related: every-brush-follows-the-pointer-with-no-lag-even (lag while painting) shares the cost of the watercolour simulation; whichever runs first should say what it changed in the other's log.
acceptance: Reproduce first in the probe at Next defaults: paint 3 to 6 strokes (watercolour and oil, large and small), pick Smudge, drag across them. MEASURE how long the canvas stops responding (main-thread stall and time until the canvas shows the smudge), and write it in the audit before any change.

After the fix: no main-thread stall over 50 ms, and each smudge drag event is shown within one 120 Hz frame at p95, with 10 strokes on the layer, MEASURED with the same harness and in the audit beside the before numbers.

Editing a paint layer never re-runs the whole watercolour or oil simulation for every earlier stroke on every tile or every frame; the audit says how many times each stroke is simulated during one smudge drag, before and after.
The finished picture is unchanged: before and after pictures of the same strokes plus smudge match within a stated tolerance.
A playtest walk paints, smudges and checks the canvas kept answering.
Logic in PhotonzRender is test-first; rendering changes carry the perf note.
Try path: Next defaults, Brush tool, three watercolour strokes at 150 pt and two oil strokes, then Smudge across them; it smears right away and the app never stops.
An audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Related user ask filed 2026-10-25: painting-is-what-you-see-earlier-strokes-never-r (earlier strokes re-simulated and swapped to a sharper copy on every new stroke; paint-layer raster cache keyed by the whole content). Likely the same root; do not fix it two different ways.

Reproduced first: smudge press 199.7 ms (5 strokes) and 419.4 ms (10 strokes) on the main thread, 17 and 32 strokes simulated per smudge. Cause: CanvasBrush mouseDown re-rasterized the whole paint layer to get the paint a smudge/wash/oil reads, and every render after the release replayed every stroke (brushes.md decision 5 was never built). Fix: PaintRasterCache (only new strokes painted onto the kept raster, byte-identical to a replay, 128 MB LRU, cleared on memory pressure, concurrent asks deduped), canvas reads at DocumentRenderer.bakeScale so it shares the render's raster, and warmBrushPaint draws the press's view-sized bitmap in the background. After: press 0.1 ms, 1 stroke simulated, longest pass 18 ms. Chose drawing the press bitmap ahead in the background over a lower-quality synchronous draw because the synchronous 12 MP draw alone was 40-55 ms.

A paint layer now keeps its last raster (PaintRasterCache, PhotonzRender, byte-identical to a full replay, 128 MB LRU, cleared under memory pressure), and a brush press reads the paint under it ready-drawn in the background (CanvasNSView.warmBrushPaint at DocumentRenderer.bakeScale). Measured with smudge-after-paint-keeps-up-walk on a 12 MP canvas: smudge press 419 ms -> 0.1 ms with ten strokes, moves 0.5 ms p95, longest main pass 18 ms, strokes simulated per smudge 32 -> 1; the walk now fails over 50 ms / 8.3 ms / 50 ms / 2 strokes. Held vs landed 0.00%. 10 brush walks and the full suite (14605 tests) green. Commit d2efecfb. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-25-smudging-after-a-few-paint-strokes-never-freezes.json.
